title: Kayla, 25: Skipping $15 Insurance Cost $4,800

scenes.say: $4,800 of Kayla's stuff was ruined, and none of it was covered.
A pipe burst upstairs. Her landlord's policy covers the building, not her things.
Laptop, bed, couch, clothes. It adds up fast.
Renters insurance often costs around $15 a month. About $180 a year.
With a $500 deductible, she'd have paid about $500, not $4,800.
That's 26 years of premiums at that price, gone in one afternoon.
Before signing a lease, she now checks three things.

items.text: Pick a deductible you can pay

scenes.say: Is your stuff covered right now? Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck, because she saved $180, and lost $4,800.

visual.text: Is your stuff covered right now?

question: Do you have renters insurance, or are you skipping it too?
description: Kayla skipped renters insurance to save about $15 a month. When a pipe burst upstairs she replaced about $4,800 of her things herself, since the landlord's policy covers the building, not tenants' belongings. Prices and deductibles vary; numbers are rounded US estimates.
